deep.reconstruction:
This page has no independent content. It is the mirror-reversed show-through, seen through the paper, of the writing on the other side of the leaf (the 'previous page', fol. 37r). Read in a mirror, the lines match that page line by line:
- '...muß v nicht die halbe Dicke der Linse sondern die ganze Dicke bezeichnen.'
- 'So gäbe mithin die Formel die Verkürzung = 7,17 Zoll.'
- 'Allein die Formel ist selbst nur eine Näherung, wobei das Quadrat von v vernachlässigt wird.'
- 'Im angeführten Beispiel ist die richtige Zahl für die Verkürzung 5,13 Zoll.'
- Then the formulas f' = f − (f f'/(k(k−v)))·n v, with the note 'v die ganze Dicke positiv genommen; k mit gehörigem Zeichen', and finally f' = f/(1 − f n v/(k(k−v))).

Content (from the recto). Gauss is correcting a paraxial focal-length formula for the thickness of a lens.
- f is the focal distance computed without thickness (thin lens).
- f' is the corrected distance.
- v is the full thickness of the lens, which Gauss stresses is not the half-thickness.
- k is a surface radius, taken with its proper sign.
- n is the refraction-related coefficient. Most likely it is n = (μ−1)/μ or similar; the exact meaning is not determinable from this page.

Steps:
1. A first-order formula, neglecting v², gives a shortening of the focal distance of 7.17 inches in a worked example from the earlier text. Gauss remarks that this formula is itself only an approximation; the exact shortening in that example is 5.13 inches.
2. He writes the correction implicitly as f' = f − f f' · n v/(k(k−v)). Here f' appears on the right, so the correction is not just a first-order term in v.
3. [My step] Write X = n v/(k(k−v)). Then f' + f f' X = f, so f' = f/(1 + f X). Equivalently 1/f' = 1/f + n v/(k(k−v)): the thickness term adds linearly to the reciprocal focal length, as in the exact paraxial thick-lens (Gullstrand-type) formula. As transcribed, the final line has a minus sign in the denominator, f/(1 − f n v/(k(k−v))). That matches the implicit formula only if the sign in the first line is actually '+', or if a sign convention for k absorbs it. The first-order expansion f/(1 ∓ fX) ≈ f ± f²X agrees with the shortening formula up to sign.
errors: The verso carries no original writing: everything visible is bleed-through of fol. 37r, reversed.

Possible sign inconsistency. f' = f − f f' X solves to f' = f/(1 + fX), but the recto's final line is transcribed as f/(1 − fX). Either one sign is misread in the faint ink, or Gauss lets the sign convention 'k mit gehörigem Zeichen' absorb it. This cannot be decided from the show-through.

results.what: Thickness correction to the paraxial focal length of a lens: a first-order shortening versus the exact value (7.17 vs 5.13 inches in an example), with the closed form f' = f/(1 ± f n v/(k(k−v))).
results.modern_name: Thick-lens focal-length formula (paraxial, with thickness term)
results.usually_credited_to: Classical paraxial optics: Cotes, Euler, Lagrange, Möbius; systematized by Gauss, Dioptrische Untersuchungen, 1841

deep.surprise_reason: This is mirror show-through of a routine thick-lens correction already on the recto, and it falls fully within Gauss's known dioptric work of 1840–41.
